technique.type.value: Elemental — commands a substance or force
Manipulation — moves or reshapes existing matter
Body — alters the user's own flesh
Construct — makes something that was not there
Condition — imposes a state or a restriction
Energy — shapes raw cursed energy with no intermediary

technique.cost.value: Trivial. Usable all day; the user forgets they are spending anything
Light. A long engagement is fine; a long day is not
Moderate. Perhaps a dozen uses before the edges start to go
Heavy. Three or four uses, then the user is noticeably slower
Severe. Twice in a fight, and the second time is a decision
Ruinous. Once. Afterwards they are a liability and know it
Uneven. Cheap in its ordinary use, ruinous in its real one

technique.limitation.value: Needs line of sight; a closed door ends it
The target must be named aloud, correctly, by a name they answer to
Needs skin contact to begin, though not to continue
Only one instance can be held at once; a second releases the first
Needs a few seconds of preparation that cannot be hidden
Does not work on anything currently alive
Whatever it does to the target, it does to the user a fraction as hard
Falls off sharply past a few metres and cannot be pushed
Works on a given target once; after that they are immune to it

technique.tell.value: A sound with no source — a struck bell, a held breath
The air goes cold enough to see
A hand sign the user has stopped noticing they make
Their pupils blow wide and stay that way until it ends
A half-second where everything nearby goes quiet
Their shadow arrives a beat late
Nothing at all, which is its own warning to anyone who knows

technique.common.principle.value: The technique moves a property from one thing to another rather than creating it. Nothing is made; something is taken from somewhere, and that somewhere is always left short
It defers a consequence rather than preventing it. Whatever was meant to happen still happens, later, and interest has accrued
It works on what a thing is called rather than what it is. Change the name and the technique changes its mind about the target
It acts only at boundaries — doorways, edges, the moment one state becomes another. In open ground it does nothing at all
Its effect scales with how closely the target is being observed, by anyone. Unwatched, it barely functions; in a crowd it is terrifying
The first use is weak and each repetition against the same target is stronger, until it is stopped or the user runs dry

technique.common.application.value: Unspectacular to watch. People who have fought the user describe it afterwards as bad luck rather than an attack
Nothing, nothing, nothing, then everything at once — it has no visible build-up and no gradual escalation
A field the user holds open and walks around inside, costing them the whole time it is up
Delivered by touch, so the user fights at a range that most sorcerers consider unwise
Set in advance across a location, then triggered. Ambush work; useless if the fight comes to them
Requires the user to keep talking to the target, which makes them maddening to fight

technique.common.extension.value: Reach — the same effect at distance, for several times the cost
Split — two targets at once, each at half strength
Hold — maintain the effect after the user stops concentrating, for a while
Invert — run the technique backwards, undoing what it did
Anchor — fix the effect to a place rather than a person
Chain — jump the effect to whoever touches the target next
Quiet — remove the tell, at a markedly higher cost
Sharpen — half the area, double the effect
Delay — set it now, let it land on a count the user chooses
Share — extend the effect to an ally, who must hold still for it

technique.common.maximum.value: Applies the technique to everything within sight at once, indiscriminately, and leaves the user unable to use it again that day
Removes the technique's usual limitation entirely for a count of ten, at a cost measured in days of recovery
Makes a single application permanent. Irreversible by the user, and they do not always find out what that means until later
Collapses every use the user has banked that day into one strike

technique.common.domain.value: A bare interior with no exits, where the technique lands automatically on everything the user looks at
A hall of standing ledgers; everything the occupants have taken is read out, and taken back
Ankle-deep water to the horizon under a white sky, where the technique costs the user nothing and everyone else moves as though wading
An incomplete domain — a barrier that will not quite close, trading the guaranteed hit for a shorter, cheaper hold
A reconstruction of a room from the user's life, rendered in too much detail, where the technique applies to anything they remember touching

technique.shikigami.principle.value: The shikigami are inherited, not created. Each one was bound by an ancestor and the user has only been handed the leash — they cannot make new ones, and cannot replace what they lose
Each shikigami must be beaten before it will answer. An unbeaten one can be attempted once; failure means it is gone for good
Every shikigami is held by a specific promise the user made. Break the promise and the shikigami is released, hostile, and knows exactly why
The user makes them from materials — paper, bone, cloth — and each one holds only as long as its body does
A shikigami exists as long as the user can state its full name without hesitating. Interrupt the name and it comes apart
Destroyed shikigami are absorbed by the survivors rather than lost; the remaining ones inherit a fragment of what died

technique.shikigami.application.value: Fights almost entirely through the shikigami, hanging back and directing. Dangerous at range, unimpressive in a corner
Holds one shikigami out at a time and swaps as the fight changes, which makes the user's read of a situation the real weapon
Fights alongside them rather than behind them, with the shikigami covering the openings the user deliberately leaves
Uses them for everything but fighting — scouting, carrying, holding doors, watching an exit all night
Brings everything out at once and accepts that it cannot be held for long

technique.shikigami.extension.value: Merge — combine two shikigami into one larger, briefer, worse-tempered thing
Ride — see and hear through a shikigami at any distance, while standing still and defenceless
Lend — hand control of one to an ally for as long as the user can see them
Sacrifice — dismiss a shikigami to cancel an incoming attack outright
Echo — summon a weaker copy that cannot act, only occupy attention
Reflex — a standing order a shikigami carries out without being called
Bind — dismiss a shikigami into a wound to close it, at the cost of the shikigami for a week
Relay — pass a message between two shikigami wherever they are

technique.shikigami.maximum.value: Every shikigami the user holds, out at once, acting independently and without further orders, for as long as the user stays conscious
The one shikigami the user has never successfully bound, called anyway. It arrives. Whether it helps is a separate question
Collapses every shikigami lost over the user's career into a single composite, which lasts one exchange and remembers how each of them died

technique.shikigami.domain.value: A walled compound at dusk, every room occupied by a shikigami that was never summoned and cannot be dismissed
A long run of kennels with the gates already open, where anything the user's shikigami have ever caught is caught again automatically
A bare parade ground where the user's shikigami are called by name in order, and each arrival strikes once before the next is named
An incomplete domain — a half-walled court that trades the guaranteed hit for summoning without cost while it holds

technique.elemental.principle.value: The user does not create the substance; they convert what is already present. In a dry room they are nearly powerless, and they are very aware of where the water is
They move heat rather than making it. Everything they warm is paid for by something nearby going cold, including, if they are careless, themselves
The effect builds in a space over time rather than arriving at once, so the user's real skill is in choosing where to stand ten minutes early
They can only act on a substance at the moment it changes state — freezing, boiling, catching, setting. Stable matter is inert to them
Output scales with how much of the substance is within reach, which makes terrain the whole fight

technique.elemental.application.value: Stands off and shapes the field, which works until something closes the distance
Used in contact, in small amounts, with precision — a palm of flame rather than a wave of it
Rarely aimed at people. Used to make ground unusable and herd the fight somewhere the user has prepared
Worn rather than thrown — a layer the user maintains over themselves and renews as it is stripped

technique.elemental.extension.value: Shape — hold the substance in a form it would not naturally take
Persist — it stays after the user stops paying for it, and stops answering to them
Seed — leave a dormant trace that activates on a condition
Strip — pull the substance out of something that was relying on it
Mirror — turn an incoming instance of the same substance back
Compress — a fraction of the volume at many times the force
Breathe — deliver it from the mouth at point-blank, which hurts

technique.elemental.maximum.value: Converts everything convertible within a city block at once, and the user has no say in what that includes
One strike, compressed past the point the substance should survive, which leaves a hole in a shape nobody can explain
Holds the substance across the whole engagement area for a full minute, during which the user cannot move

technique.elemental.domain.value: A horizonless expanse of the substance itself, in which the user needs no conversion and everyone else is simply inside it
The inside of a working furnace, where every surface is already at the point of change the technique needs
A flooded street at night, the water waist-high and rising at a rate the occupants can calculate
An incomplete domain — the substance saturates the area without a sure hit, cheaper and survivable

technique.manipulation.principle.value: Anything the user has touched once can be moved as though still held
Movement is transferred: whatever the user does, the target does a beat later
The user owns one property of an object — its weight, its direction, its grain — and nothing else
What is already in motion can be redirected, but never started or stopped
The user's own gestures are performed at a distance, by nothing visible

technique.manipulation.application.value: Small, precise and unnerving: doors, blades and limbs move with no hand on them
Broad and crude — whole objects thrown about, with no fine control at all
Invisible until it matters, then a room's worth of things all move at once
Slow. Everything it does takes a few seconds, and is unstoppable in that time

technique.manipulation.extension.value: Thread Count — several objects at once, one per finger
Dead Weight — makes a held thing refuse to be let go of
Follow Through — a strike continues after the arm has stopped
Handoff — passes control of a moving object to a surface
Reversal — sends a thrown thing back along its own path
Still Hand — holds one object perfectly fixed in the air
Secondhand Strike — an object the user touched hours ago attacks now
Tangle — makes two moving things collide

technique.manipulation.maximum.value: Maximum: Every Hand At Once — everything the user has touched today moves in one motion
Maximum: The Whole Room — nothing within sight stays where it is put
Maximum: Last Gesture — one strike repeated by every object that has ever carried it

technique.manipulation.domain.value: Domain: The Workshop With No Workman — a room where every tool is already in use
Domain: A Thousand Small Obediences — nothing inside moves of its own accord
Domain: The Hall of Hands — the walls themselves reach
Domain: Marionette Theatre — everyone inside moves as the user moves

technique.body.principle.value: The user's body can be rearranged — joints, reach, density — within the same total mass
Injury is deferred rather than taken, and comes due all at once later
The user hardens on contact, and only where contact is made
Flesh can be spent as a resource: a wound given is a strike improved
The body remembers every shape it has held and can return to any of them

technique.body.application.value: Close, brutal and fast, with the technique only visible at the moment of impact
Grotesque to watch — limbs lengthening, joints inverting, nothing staying put
Nearly invisible: they simply do not break when they should
Methodical. They set up the body they will need before the fight starts

technique.body.extension.value: Overreach — one limb longer for one strike
Ballast — doubles their own weight where they stand
Grain — hardens a single point of contact to stone
Spare Joint — a bend where no bend should be
Unmade Hand — unmakes a grip on them, including their own
Debt Taken — shrugs off a wound now and feels it in a minute
Low Gear — slower, and impossible to move
Second Wind — resets the body to the shape it started in

technique.body.maximum.value: Maximum: Account Settled — every deferred injury discharged into one blow
Maximum: The Whole Frame — the body remade for exactly one purpose, briefly
Maximum: Unbroken — nothing lands at all for as long as they can hold it

technique.body.domain.value: Domain: The Anatomy Theatre — every wound inside is shown before it is dealt
Domain: A Body For Every Occasion — the user is whatever the fight requires
Domain: The Quarry — everything inside, flesh included, is stone
Domain: Standing Room Only — nothing inside may yield or give way

technique.space.principle.value: Two surfaces the user has touched become the same surface
Distance is borrowed from a stride not yet taken, and repaid in exhaustion
Space can be folded but not removed: what is shortened here is lengthened there
The user occupies the place they were a moment ago as readily as the place they are
Any gap can be closed, provided something of the user is already on the far side

technique.space.application.value: Disorienting. They are never quite where the eye last put them
Architectural — rooms stop connecting the way the building says they do
Economical: one step, in the only direction that mattered
Visibly costly. Every fold leaves them a little further behind themselves

technique.space.extension.value: Borrowed Step — one stride of distance, repaid immediately
Arrears — several strides at once, repaid over the following minute
Standstill — gives distance away, pinning themselves to deny it to another
Seam — joins two walls they have both touched
The Long Corridor — makes a short room take a minute to cross
Back Three — returns to where they stood three seconds ago
Threshold — a door that opens only for them
Shortfall — a strike that lands from further away than the arm reaches

technique.space.maximum.value: Maximum: Debt Called In — every borrowed stride of the fight collapses into one
Maximum: No Distance At All — for a moment, everywhere in sight is arm's reach
Maximum: The Fold — two places made one, and whatever was in both is in both

technique.space.domain.value: Domain: The Long Hallway With No Doors — distance without arrival
Domain: Everywhere Is Here — no gap inside is more than a step
Domain: The Folded Room — the inside is larger than the outside and gets larger
Domain: Return to Sender — every movement ends where it began

technique.perception.principle.value: The user perceives one chosen thing perfectly and everything else poorly
Anything that has been seen in a place can be seen again, in order
Intention is legible a moment before it becomes movement
What the user is told, they know to be true or false, and nothing more
Attention itself is detectable: they know when they are being looked for

technique.perception.application.value: Quiet and unspectacular, and it decides fights before they are joined
Invasive — they answer questions nobody asked aloud
Narrow. Extraordinary within its one sense, nearly blind outside it
Gradual: each minute on site tells them more than the last

technique.perception.extension.value: Replay — the last minute in this room, as it happened
Tell — names the next move a beat before it is made
Headcount — every living thing within a street, counted
Lie Line — knows when a thing said is believed by the speaker
Thread — follows one person's path backwards through a building
Blindside — perceives what is behind them as clearly as in front
Deep Water — finds the lowest, oldest thing in a place
Borrowed Eyes — sees from a surface they have marked

technique.perception.maximum.value: Maximum: Everything At Once — total perception, and no capacity left to act on it
Maximum: The Whole Account — the complete history of one object, in an instant
Maximum: Foreknown — the next ten seconds, seen and unchangeable

technique.perception.domain.value: Domain: Nothing Hidden — inside, every concealment fails, the user's included
Domain: The Reading Room — the past of the place plays continuously
Domain: Under Observation — every intention is announced before it acts
Domain: The Lantern — nothing inside casts a shadow

technique.barrier.principle.value: A boundary can be drawn anywhere the user can see, and holds until they look away
What is enclosed cannot be reached from outside, and cannot reach out
The barrier is not solid — it is a condition the crossing must satisfy
Walls are cheap and small; one large one costs more than twenty small
Anything written can be made binding within the space it is written in

technique.barrier.application.value: Patient and positional. They lose fights they cannot prepare for
Fast and improvised — small walls thrown up a half-second at a time
Administrative, almost: conditions declared aloud and immediately true
Invisible until something tries to cross and simply does not

technique.barrier.extension.value: Shutter — one flat wall, hand-sized, exactly where a strike was going
Hemline — a boundary along the floor that nothing may step over
Quiet Room — a space no sound enters or leaves
Toll — a crossing allowed only to those who give something up
Lantern Line — a boundary that is visible, as a warning
Lid — encloses a small thing completely, and holds it
Standing Gate — one doorway that stays open in a sealed space
Clause — a written condition the space itself enforces

technique.barrier.maximum.value: Maximum: The Sealed Ward — a district closed, at ruinous cost, for one minute
Maximum: Nothing Crosses — one boundary nothing may pass, including the user
Maximum: Every Wall At Once — all barriers drawn today, restored and reinforced

technique.barrier.domain.value: Domain: The Room With Four Doors And No Keys — inside, every exit is a condition
Domain: Terms and Conditions — the user's stated rules hold absolutely within
Domain: The Held Breath — nothing inside may move until something is given
Domain: Inside the Envelope — the boundary is the attack

technique.construct.principle.value: Cursed energy can be shaped into objects, which last until struck
What the user builds from materials on site is stronger than what they build from nothing
Anything broken can be rebuilt once, wrongly, and the wrongness is useful
The user makes tools, never weapons — and uses the tools as weapons
Constructs persist while the user does not look at them, and fail when they do

technique.construct.application.value: Slow to start, overwhelming once established. Give them a minute and lose
Improvised and ugly — whatever is lying about, assembled wrong and working
Elegant, brittle things: beautiful, and gone in one hit
Industrial. They produce the same construct, reliably, forever

technique.construct.extension.value: Brace — a strut that holds a collapsing thing up
Nail — a spike driven through two things, joining them
Hand Tool — a simple implement, perfectly suited, lasting one use
Scaffold — a structure to stand on, where there was nothing
Standing Figure — a crude body that absorbs one strike
Rebuild — a broken object reassembled, wrongly, and sharper for it
Clamp — fixes two surfaces together permanently
Offcut — a small construct made from the waste of a larger one

technique.construct.maximum.value: Maximum: The Whole Workshop — everything the user could build, built at once
Maximum: Standing Army — every construct made today, restored and animate
Maximum: The Finished Thing — one construct, perfect, permanent, and enormously costly

technique.construct.domain.value: Domain: The Yard — inside, the user's constructs replace themselves as they break
Domain: Everything Already Made — the space is full of finished work
Domain: The Patient Builder — time inside runs long enough to build anything
Domain: Scrapheap — everything inside is material, the opponent included

technique.condition.principle.value: The user declares a rule aloud, and it holds for as long as they keep to it too
A condition imposed on another must be matched by one the user accepts
What is counted can be bound: debts, strikes, words, steps
Anything agreed to, however casually, becomes mechanically true
A technique already in progress can be ended, at the cost of one of the user's own

technique.condition.application.value: Conversational and lethal — they fight by talking, and mean every word
Formal: conditions stated precisely, because imprecision costs them
Ruthless bookkeeping. They know exactly what everyone owes
Restrained. They impose one condition and win on it

technique.condition.extension.value: First Clause — one simple rule, binding on both, lasting a minute
Tally — counts strikes, and repays the total at once
Forfeit — takes something from whoever breaks the stated rule
Quietus — ends an active technique, and one of the user's own with it
Standing Debt — a condition that compounds while unresolved
Mute Clause — forbids one named action within earshot
Handshake — a willing agreement, stronger than an imposed one
Small Print — a second condition nobody noticed being stated

technique.condition.maximum.value: Maximum: Terms Enforced — every condition stated today, all binding at once
Maximum: The Unbreakable Clause — one rule nothing present can violate
Maximum: Account Closed — all debts owed to the user, collected together

technique.condition.domain.value: Domain: Court In Session — inside, the user's rules are the physics
Domain: Nothing Said Is Idle — every word spoken inside binds its speaker
Domain: The Ledger — nothing inside may act while it owes
Domain: Signed and Witnessed — one agreement, inescapable while it stands

technique.information.principle.value: Names are handles: knowing one truly gives purchase on its owner
Information the user holds can be given away, and is lost in the giving
Any object will say where it has been and who held it
What is widely believed becomes marginally true within earshot
The user can reach any mind they have a name for, once, briefly

technique.information.application.value: Non-combative and dreaded. They win before anyone draws
Social: they fight through other people, who do not know they are being used
Archival. They turn up knowing things nobody told them
Transactional — they trade what they know, and it is always a fair price

technique.information.extension.value: Provenance — an object's last three owners, in order
Cold Call — one sentence delivered into a named person's attention
Hearsay — plants a belief that spreads on its own
Index — locates every copy of a named thing nearby
Loose Talk — makes a person say what they most want to keep
Chain — follows a name to everyone who has used it
Receipt — proves an event happened, to anyone shown it
Redaction — removes one fact from everyone present

technique.information.maximum.value: Maximum: Full Disclosure — everything the user knows, made known to all present
Maximum: The Whole Record — one person's history, complete and undeniable
Maximum: Named and Numbered — every curse within the district, located at once

technique.information.domain.value: Domain: Nothing Is Private — every fact inside is available to everyone inside
Domain: The Reading Room — the user knows the answer to any question asked within
Domain: On The Record — nothing said or done inside can later be denied
Domain: The Long Memory — the place's whole past, present and insistent

technique.energy.principle.value: Cursed energy can be moved between things, but never created
The user burns only cursed energy — flesh is untouched, technique is not
What the user takes they must spend immediately or lose
Energy can be stored in objects and withdrawn later, at a loss
Their own output can be spent as a lump rather than metered

technique.energy.application.value: Attritional. They do not win exchanges; they make exchanges unaffordable
Flashy and expensive — enormous output, very little left afterwards
Parasitic: the longer the fight, the stronger they are and the weaker you are
Measured. They spend exactly what the moment needs and nothing more

technique.energy.extension.value: Cold Flame — a fire that consumes cursed energy and nothing else
Low Tide — draws energy out of a technique mid-use
Reserve — banks output in a held object for later
Siphon — takes a little from everything within reach
Dead Air — a space where output costs double
Discharge — everything banked, released at once, undirected
Dry Season — denies a target their own reserves for a few seconds

technique.energy.maximum.value: Maximum: Everything At Once — the whole reserve spent in a single expression
Maximum: Nothing Left — drains every cursed thing present, the user included
Maximum: The Long Burn — sustained output far past what the body should allow

technique.energy.domain.value: Domain: The Cold Hearth — inside, cursed energy drains towards the user
Domain: Nothing Burns But This — no technique but the user's functions within
Domain: Dry Season — output inside costs several times what it should
Domain: The Furnace — everything inside is fuel
